@Xichen96 — update after re-reviewing current head `5fd3dfd9`: this is still not ready to merge.

- The branch now conflicts with master/#114, so the existing green build is stale.
- Family enablement is inferred only from interface addresses; configured relay-family intent is not passed to the daemon. A dual-stack SVI configured for one family can start both monitors and create false health/repair signals.

@StormLiangMS We addressed the current-head feedback:

1. **Family availability lifecycle:** DHCPmon evaluates family availability only at startup; later configuration changes require restart. Dynamic configuration subscription is a separate project and is outside this PR.
2. **Source-level coverage:** The requested lifecycle matrix and failure-injection coverage require new `sonic-dhcpmon` unit-test infrastructure, which is too large for this PR. The gap is on our radar as a separate project.
3. **Loopback0 LLA:** Agreed. `giaddr_ipv6_lla` was not consumed by any active check profile. The current head removes the unused Loopback0/giaddr IPv6 LLA state and passes `NULL` for that optional accessor output while preserving downstream `vlan_ipv6_lla`.
4. **Disabled-family status APIs:** Agreed. `dhcp_device_print_status()` now guards the applicable socket pair before accessing `sock_map`, so a future ungated call cannot reach `sock_map.at(-1)`.
5. **Persisted family state:** Agreed as a follow-up. Distinguishing disabled from enabled-but-idle requires a separate observability contract whose scope may span the producer and consumer repositories.
6. **Restacking:** The final reviewed change is squashed to one commit and rebased onto current master, including the merged overlapping changes from https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/96 and https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/99.

Current head: `c16ef8c98fd7ce66837f3e77ad8457683f21b11e`.

@StormLiangMS Here is the design reasoning behind the current boundary.

We are working toward one long-running `dhcpmon` process that handles configuration refresh, multiple VLANs, and both IPv4 and IPv6. In that model, the daemon should consume the authoritative CONFIG_DB state and dynamically reconcile VLAN, family, upstream-interface, and Loopback0 changes.

Passing configured-family intent through supervisor command-line parameters would be a detour from that design. It would:

- create a second, startup-only source of configuration truth;
- require supervisor regeneration and process restart after configuration changes;
- reinforce the current process-per-VLAN model;
- require another redesign when multi-VLAN dynamic reconciliation moves into the daemon.

That is why https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/111 is intentionally limited to separating the IPv4 and IPv6 lifecycles. One unavailable family no longer prevents the other from starting, while the existing passive-monitoring behavior remains unchanged.

The planned sequence is:

1. This PR establishes independent IPv4/IPv6 capability.
2. https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/27277 consumes the propagated source and supplies the correct VLAN and upstream rendering, including IPv6-only operation.
3. The follow-up configuration-refresh work consolidates monitoring into one process and dynamically manages multiple VLANs, both families, and late address changes.

The late Dual-ToR Loopback0 case follows the same reasoning. Today, family availability is intentionally a startup snapshot and later address changes require restart. A one-off startup flag or retry path would not provide the dynamic reconciliation the final design needs.

I believe keeping this prerequisite focused and avoiding a temporary external-parameter interface is the cleaner design. However, this is a design tradeoff, and I will follow your final judgment if you prefer immediate configured-family gating despite the expected later rework.

@StormLiangMS @ashutosh-agrawal This PR is ready for review on the current head. Xichen review, exact-head CI, and required validation are complete; please review when available.

@StormLiangMS The branch is now rebased onto merged [#114](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/114) at head `42479fc77f0f21209e07f460ca0788e7ee828033`.

The only conflict was in `timeout_callback()`. The resolution preserves #114's counter-synchronization and post-sync snapshot handling, then applies this PR's IPv4/IPv6 enablement gates to the debug-counter output. The other eight changed files retain the identical isolated patch ID, and the branch remains one root commit.

Exact-head Azure build [1210811](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1210811) passed on amd64, arm64, and armhf; DCO and EasyCLA passed. The configured-family and startup-lifecycle design boundary remains documented in [the earlier response](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/111#issuecomment-5390960921).

Please review the current head and make the final design judgment.

@Xichen96 - re-reviewed exact head `42479fc77f0f21209e07f460ca0788e7ee828033`.

**No new blocking code issue found within the documented startup-snapshot scope.** I am narrowing my earlier review, not treating the deferred configuration/lifecycle work as implemented.

- **Previous implementation concerns:** this head is directly based on merged #114, and its counter-synchronization skip/post-sync snapshot logic is preserved. The IPv6 VLAN GUA+LLA requirement and per-family DualToR Loopback prerequisites are consistent. Disabled-family socket/status/health paths are gated, partial socket-open failures unwind the opened descriptors, and disabled-family cache-completion writes use the existing DB synchronization mutex.
- **Design judgment:** I recommend keeping this prerequisite scoped to independent-family startup, rather than requiring a temporary configured-family CLI or a live configuration-reconciliation implementation here. A dual-stack SVI can still monitor both families regardless of configured relay-family intent; that was already the behavior for successful dual-stack startup in the base, not a new regression introduced by this split. Late/missing addresses are still a real limitation: a family disabled at startup does not become monitored when its addresses appear later without restarting dhcpmon.
- **Correction to my earlier wording:** the monitor publishes a disparity event; I did not find an automatic repair/restart action in that path. Calling these "repair signals" overstated what this daemon does.

This is a source-review conclusion, not end-to-end rollout sign-off. The downstream process matrix in sonic-net/sonic-mgmt#26657 still needs an image containing sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#27277; actual single-family packet/counter behavior and restart/clear-counter integration remain downstream validation work. The IPv6 relay-health transformation fix is also the separate #101 change, not part of this head.
Original PR: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/87

@Xichen96 — re-review of **`de554e95291b0d9bdeac8711d168d5e782fd782e`**: **no remaining blocking issue found; the earlier approval hold is addressed.**

- The head is directly based on `d8bd782`, the merged #114 synchronization fix. I checked the synchronization skip/main-thread snapshot-rebase path. The new [`get_counter_delta()`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/blob/de554e95291b0d9bdeac8711d168d5e782fd782e/src/dhcp_device.cpp#L126-L132) also clamps decreases to zero, and the new message groups use `int[]` without the earlier enum-pointer casts.
- The DHCPv6 transformations correctly distinguish forward and reply activity, including nested relays, require both directions when both have RX activity, and do not impose an invalid one-to-one count requirement on server fan-out. IPv4 logic is unchanged.
- I independently confirmed that final head `de554e9` and hardware-validated `9cb95c8` have the identical Git tree `c111435bcb16ade394a467f27eae4b100d1aa4bd`. The [posted master/202605 evidence](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/101#issuecomment-5530368891) addresses the earlier validation request, including synchronization protection and disparity thresholds. Those hardware runs/artifact hashes are author-provided evidence, not runs independently repeated here.

Local verification compiled the exact counter-helper and alert/threshold bodies in an isolated C++ harness: **56 checks passed**, covering valid/invalid transformations, both-direction combinations, idle traffic, counter decreases/rollover, unchanged IPv4 behavior, and first/next disparity events at **198/216 seconds**. The source publishes an event; it does not automatically repair/restart the relay. This was a focused replay with counter/event dependencies stubbed, not a full Linux daemon build or DUT run.

**Current CI / DCO / CLA:** green, including final-head build 1211003 on amd64, arm64, and armhf. Ready for approval from this review; this is a new comment only, **no approval submitted**.

@Xichen96 I reviewed the current head `012c6508368b88a171b65b382091c6cc6fc837cb`. The per-edge refactor and quiet-parent/moving-child comparison look good, but I found one issue I think should be fixed before merge.

**Idle windows reset a real mismatch streak.**

`check_aggregate_health()` returns `DHCP_MON_STATUS_HEALTHY` when neither the parent nor aggregate counter advances. `check_dhcp_relay_health()` then resets `state.count` to zero for `HEALTHY`.

On a broken low-traffic edge, the sequence can be:

1. A DHCP retry advances only the child aggregate: `UNHEALTHY`, count becomes 1.
2. The next 18-second window has no packets: both sides idle, `HEALTHY`, count resets to 0.
3. A later retry starts again from 1.

The mismatch can therefore never pass the default threshold unless it occurs for 11 consecutive non-idle windows. This is especially relevant to the frozen-parent/moving-child failure mode this PR newly detects; the old category behavior did not reliably detect that case in the first place.

Could the both-sides-idle branch return `DHCP_MON_STATUS_INDETERMINATE` instead? The existing `INDETERMINATE` handling preserves an active streak through quiet windows while not starting a streak when the count is zero.

Non-blocking follow-ups: validate the inherited VLAN-TX member-count ratio for unicast OFFER/ACK traffic, and add focused tests for idle/match/mismatch/multi-member ratio cases.

## Code Review

### Critical

1. **`src/packet_handler.cpp` — `find_dhcpv6_option` / `dhcpv6_sanity_check`**: Off-by-one in DHCPv6 option parsing. The boundary check `while (offset + 1 < dhcp6_options_sz)` only ensures 2 bytes exist, but 4 bytes are immediately read (code at `offset`, len at `offset+2`). If only 2–3 bytes remain, `ntohs(*(uint16_t *)(dhcp6_options + offset + 2))` is an out-of-bounds read. Should be `offset + 4 <= dhcp6_options_sz`. Same pattern in `dhcpv6_sanity_check`.

2. **`src/packet_handler.cpp` — `ipv6_sanity_check`**: IPv6 extension header traversal bug. When the loop finds `nxt_hdr[0] == IPPROTO_UDP`, it advances the pointer *past* the UDP header with `nxt_hdr += (nxt_hdr[1] + 1) * 8` before returning. The returned pointer points to data *after* the actual UDP header. Should return `(struct udphdr *)nxt_hdr` immediately after confirming IPPROTO_UDP, without the extra advance.

3. **`src/dhcp_mon.cpp` — `db_counters_initialized`**: `mCountersDbPtr->hget(...)` returns `std::shared_ptr<std::string>`. The code assigns to `std::string *field = ... .get()` extracting the raw pointer, but the `shared_ptr` is destroyed at the semicolon, leaving `field` as a dangling pointer. The subsequent `field->empty()` is use-after-free. Store the `shared_ptr` in a local variable to keep it alive.

4. **`src/dhcp_device.cpp` — `dhcp_device_check_positive_health`**: Unsafe cast `(const int *)monitored_msgs` where `monitored_msgs` is `const dhcp_message_type_t[]` (enum). Underlying type of unscoped enums is implementation-defined. Should use a properly typed array or explicit conversion.

### High

5. **`src/sock_mgr.cpp` — `sock_mgr_start_event_loop`**: Thread lambda captures `info` by reference from a range-based for loop over `sock_map` (an `unordered_map`). If the map is rehashed, all references become dangling. Capture by value or look up by key.

6. **`src/dhcp_device.cpp` — `initialize_intf_mac_and_ip_addr`**: Requires exactly 1 IPv4, 1 IPv6 GUA, and 1 IPv6 LLA on every interface. This is overly strict — some interfaces (e.g. loopback) may legitimately lack an address type. Will cause init failures on valid configurations.

7. **`src/packet_handler.cpp` — `callback_common`**: `debug_mask` is set as thread-local but modified without RAII guard. If `packet_handler` throws, `debug_mask` is never restored. Use an RAII pattern.

### Medium

8. **`src/sock_mgr.cpp` — `sock_mgr_drain_sock_buffer`**: Stack buffer `char buf[65536]` is 64KB on the stack. Could cause stack overflow on constrained systems. Use heap allocation or existing sock_info buffers.

9. **`src/packet_handler.h` — `DHCPV6_OPTION_CODE_MAX = 150`**: Hardcoded limit is arbitrary. IANA assigns DHCPv6 option codes up to ~200+ and growing. This will reject legitimate packets with newer option codes. Should be set much higher or removed.

10. **`src/dhcp_check_profile.h`**: `std::unordered_map` with enum keys relies on implicit hash support from GCC, which isn't guaranteed by the standard. Consider `std::map` or defining a custom hash.

11. **`objects.mk`**: `-levent` appears twice in the LIBS line. Harmless but indicates sloppy dependency management.

---

Overall the architectural refactoring (pcap filters, modular `sock_mgr`/`packet_handler`/`health_check`/`dhcp_check_profile`) looks solid and the DHCPv6 protocol handling (relay-forward/reply, link-addr) is generally correct. **Items 1–3 are must-fix before merge** — they can cause crashes or memory corruption on crafted packets.

Thanks for the thorough review. Here's the status of each item:

Critical

1. Off-by-one in find_dhcpv6_option / dhcpv6_sanity_check Fixed in e73a9a2. Changed find_dhcpv6_option to offset + 3 < dhcp6_options_sz to ensure the full 4-byte option header is available. dhcpv6_sanity_check was already safe — it reads the 2-byte type code first, then has a secondary guard if (offset + 3 >= dhcp6_options_sz) before reading the length.
Added comments to both functions documenting the boundary checks at each step.

2. IPv6 extension header traversal in ipv6_sanity_check The code is correct. When the loop finds nxt_hdr[0] == IPPROTO_UDP, nxt_hdr points at the last extension header whose next-header field indicates UDP follows. The advance nxt_hdr += (nxt_hdr[1] + 1) * 8 skips past this extension header to reach the actual UDP header. Without this advance, we'd return
a pointer to the extension header, not the UDP header. Added a comment clarifying this in dece900.

3. Dangling pointer in db_counters_initialized Fixed in 7a7528f. Stored the shared_ptr in local variables instead of extracting the raw pointer via .get(). Also cleaned up an unnecessary .get() call at another hget site and added a comment explaining why shared_ptr keeps the string alive.

4. Unsafe enum cast (const int *)monitored_msgs Intentional. The helper functions (check_counter_not_transmitted, check_counter_increased, check_counters_delta_expected) use const int * to accept both dhcp_message_type_t and dhcpv6_message_type_t arrays without duplicating the function for each enum type. Safe on all SONiC platforms (GCC/Linux) where
unscoped enums use int as the underlying type. Added a comment in 09157c7.

High

5. Thread captures reference in sock_mgr_start_event_loop Safe in current code — sock_map is fully populated before sock_mgr_start_event_loop and never modified afterward. Added a comment warning that the map must not be modified after this point in e630b0e.

6. Overly strict initialize_intf_mac_and_ip_addr Intentional. dhcpmon requires IPv4, IPv6 GUA, and IPv6 LLA on each monitored interface for packet validation in the check profiles (src/dst IP matching). All interfaces passed to dhcpmon (-id, -iu, -im) are expected to have all address types in a properly configured SONiC DHCP relay setup. The loopback
interface call has its own separate handling.

7. debug_mask no RAII guard in callback_common Safe without RAII. The packet handlers (packet_handler, packet_handler_v6) are void functions with internal error handling — they do not throw. Even if debug_mask were stuck at false, the next loop iteration resets it. Added a comment in 54a3a61.

Medium

8. 64KB stack buffer in sock_mgr_drain_sock_buffer Acceptable. This is a drain function called once during init, not recursively. The default Linux stack size is 8MB. 64KB is well within limits for all SONiC platforms.

9. Hardcoded DHCPV6_OPTION_CODE_MAX = 150 Kept at 150 based on current IANA assignments. Added a reference to the IANA DHCPv6 parameters registry in 40472cd. (https://www.iana.org/assignments/dhcpv6-parameters/dhcpv6-parameters.xhtml)

10. unordered_map with enum keys Works on all SONiC platforms. GCC supports std::hash for unscoped enums via implicit conversion to the underlying integer type (C++14+). No portability concern for SONiC.

11. Duplicate -levent in LIBS Fixed in 583c73e.
